title: tune-nccl-streams-and-scheduling-for-tensor-parallel-overlap
author: Rajat Mehra
release_notes: Performance: Improved NCCL comm/compute overlap for tensor-parallel runs — up to 18% p99 latency reduction and 22% throughput increase in internal TP benchmarks. No API changes.
description: Motivation: tensor-parallel multi-GPU workloads were spending significant time idle waiting for collectives, especially at medium sequence lengths. This PR tunes NCCL stream usage, stream priorities, and the runtime scheduling path to increase overlap between GPU compute kernels and NCCL collectives. Approach: 1) introduce a dual-stream model in the runtime: a prioritized communication stream and a default compute stream; 2) add a lightweight StreamPool that reuses CUDA streams with configured priorities instead of creating/destroying streams per request; 3) schedule collectives via a new NCCLScheduler that groups small collectives and issues them on the comm stream with ordering fences to avoid kernel/collective races; 4) add tiny synchronization points (cudaEvent) to ensure correct ordering without global stalls; 5) adjust kernel launch priorities and prefer asynchronous kernel launches when K/V cache hits allow immediate continuation; 6) expose two new runtime knobs (runtime.nccl_comm_priority and runtime.stream_pool_size) with safe defaults. Testing & validation: microbench (redwood/benchmark-lab) showed steady 12-18% p99 reduction across TP=2..8; end-to-end canary in perf-canary improved throughput by ~22% on our representative chat workload while keeping token-level latency within SLO. Safety: changes are opt-in via runtime flags for Dedicated/Private customers and behind a feature toggle for hosted rollout. Checklist: - [x] design doc + perf plan (linked in PR discussion) - [x] unit tests for StreamPool and NCCLScheduler - [x] microbench results attached - [x] canary rollout + metrics validation - [x] documentation update (docs/notes/perf/nccl-tuning.md) Related work: builds on prior PRs that tuned NCCL scheduling and collectives (see ENG-1722, PRs 26432/27188 in repo). Impact: no user-facing API change; operational knobs for platform operators. Follow-ups: evaluate cudaGraph capture for recurrent workloads, and evaluate dynamic stream sizing for peak burst scenarios.

review_comments: Asha Patel: Nice work. Two questions: 1) have you validated behavior on NVLink vs PCIe topologies? 2) can we reduce the default stream_pool_size for small instances?

Author (Rajat): We ran the microbench on both NVLink DGX-like (4x A100 NVLink) and on PCIe multi-socket instances; NVLink showed slightly better absolute improvement but similar relative gains. Default pool is 4 per-GPU; reduced to 2 on small instance profiles as suggested via runtime config.

Miguel Santos: There's a race I hit while running stress tests — a kernel sometimes writes to a buffer while an ordered collective is pending. Can you add a lightweight cudaEvent-based fence around that path?
Author (Rajat): Good catch. Added a cudaEvent fence and explicitly wait on the comm stream before issuing dependent kernels. Added unit test to catch regression.
Lena Fischer: CI perf check flaked once (timing variance). Did a rerun and it passed. Approving after verifying canary dashboards.
Author: Thank you — addressed comments and added documentation on how to tune comm priority and stream pool size for Dedicated customers.
canary_notes: Canary rolled to 5% of traffic for 24h. Metrics: token throughput +22% (median), p99 latency -18% for mid-sequence workloads. No error increase observed. Rollout plan in docs updated.
perf_results: GPU idle time reduced by ~30% in mixed-length synthetic traces
backcompat_notes: No breaking API changes. Runtime flags default to previous behavior if feature toggle is off.
